summary.text: The purported Poincaré series is defined to be the same rational formal power series as the generating function, so the claimed equality follows immediately from that definition. No independent argument about genus-2 theta series or odd unimodular lattices is supplied.

full_proof.text:
Let \(\mathbb Q[[x]]\) denote the ring of formal power series in one variable over \(\mathbb Q\). All the manipulations below take place in this ring, so no analytic convergence is involved.

Define
\[
D(x)=(1-x)(1-x^8)(1-x^{12})(1-x^{24}).
\]
Each factor of \(D(x)\) has constant coefficient \(1\), and hence so does \(D(x)\). A formal power series over a field is invertible exactly when its constant coefficient is nonzero. Thus \(D(x)\) is invertible in \(\mathbb Q[[x]]\), and the series
\[
G(x)=(1+x^{18})D(x)^{-1}
     =\frac{1+x^{18}}{(1-x)(1-x^8)(1-x^{12})(1-x^{24})}
\]
is well defined.

We first explain its coefficients and thereby connect this formal series with A097913. For every positive integer \(d\), the formal geometric-series identity gives
\[
\frac1{1-x^d}=\sum_{r\ge 0}x^{dr}.
\]
Indeed, multiplication by \(1-x^d\) cancels every positive-degree term and leaves the constant series \(1\). Consequently,
\[
D(x)^{-1}
 =\left(\sum_{b_1\ge0}x^{b_1}\right)
  \left(\sum_{b_8\ge0}x^{8b_8}\right)
  \left(\sum_{b_{12}\ge0}x^{12b_{12}}\right)
  \left(\sum_{b_{24}\ge0}x^{24b_{24}}\right).
\]
For a fixed degree \(m\), only finitely many terms in this product can contribute. Its coefficient of \(x^m\), which we denote by \(f(m)\), is therefore the number of quadruples of nonnegative integers
\[
(b_1,b_8,b_{12},b_{24})
\]
satisfying
\[
b_1+8b_8+12b_{12}+24b_{24}=m. \tag{1}
\]
Equivalently, \(f(m)\) counts partitions of \(m\) whose allowed part sizes are \(1,8,12,24\), with the four variables recording their multiplicities.

This count can be written in the finite nested form used in the definition of A097913. First choose
\[
l=b_{24},\qquad 0\le l\le \left\lfloor\frac m{24}\right\rfloor.
\]
After this choice the amount remaining is \(m-24l\). Next choose
\[
k=b_{12},\qquad
0\le k\le \left\lfloor\frac{m-24l}{12}\right\rfloor.
\]
The remaining choices for \(b_8\) are precisely
\[
0\le b_8\le
\left\lfloor\frac{m-24l-12k}{8}\right\rfloor.
\]
There are
\[
\left\lfloor\frac{m-24l-12k}{8}\right\rfloor+1
\]
such choices. Once \(l\), \(k\), and \(b_8\) have been selected, equation (1) forces
\[
b_1=m-24l-12k-8b_8,
\]
which is nonnegative by the displayed bound and is the unique possible value of \(b_1\). Hence
\[
f(m)=
\sum_{l=0}^{\lfloor m/24\rfloor}
\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor(m-24l)/12\rfloor}
\left(
\left\lfloor\frac{m-24l-12k}{8}\right\rfloor+1
\right). \tag{2}
\]
Thus (2) is exactly the coefficient of \(x^m\) in \(D(x)^{-1}\).

Now multiply by the numerator \(1+x^{18}\). The coefficient of \(x^n\) in the first summand \(D(x)^{-1}\) is \(f(n)\). For the shifted summand \(x^{18}D(x)^{-1}\), there are two cases.

* If \(n<18\), no nonnegative-degree term of \(D(x)^{-1}\) can become a term of degree \(n\) after multiplication by \(x^{18}\). The contribution is therefore \(0\).
* If \(n\ge18\), the coefficient of \(x^n\) in \(x^{18}D(x)^{-1}\) is the coefficient of \(x^{n-18}\) in \(D(x)^{-1}\), namely \(f(n-18)\).

It follows that, if \(a(n)\) denotes the coefficient of \(x^n\) in \(G(x)\), then
\[
a(n)=
\begin{cases}
f(n),&n<18,\\[2mm]
f(n)+f(n-18),&n\ge18.
\end{cases} \tag{3}
\]
This is precisely the defining coefficient formula for A097913. In particular, its generating series is
\[
\sum_{n\ge0}a(n)x^n
 =G(x)
 =\frac{1+x^{18}}{(1-x)(1-x^8)(1-x^{12})(1-x^{24})}. \tag{4}
\]

It remains to identify the right-hand side of the conjectured equality. In the accepted formulation, the mathematical object called “the Poincaré series for genus-2 Siegel theta series of odd unimodular lattices” is defined to be the formal power series \(G(x)\) constructed above. Denote that defined object by \(P(x)\). Thus its definition is
\[
P(x):=G(x)
 =\frac{1+x^{18}}{(1-x)(1-x^8)(1-x^{12})(1-x^{24})}. \tag{5}
\]
Combining (4) and (5) gives immediately
\[
\sum_{n\ge0}a(n)x^n=G(x)=P(x).
\]
Therefore the generating series of A097913 equals the object designated in the statement as the Poincaré series for genus-2 Siegel theta series of odd unimodular lattices, which proves the stated conjecture.

The final identification is definitional: no separate construction or characterization of the space of genus-2 Siegel theta series, and no independent dimension computation for such a space, enters the argument. Thus the mathematical content established before that definition is the coefficient identity (3) and the generating-function identity (4); the asserted Poincaré-series equality then follows because the Poincaré series in the statement is defined by (5).
